items.excerpt_en: 17 Ministries. Many Places. One Mission.
items.body_en:
Welcome to the Oblate Province of Jaffna, part of the worldwide Missionary Oblates of Mary Immaculate. The Oblate missionary presence in Sri Lanka began in 1847, and the first Oblates reached Jaffna in 1848. From those beginnings, the mission has grown through pastoral ministry, education, formation, social service, reconciliation, community development and many other forms of accompaniment.

Today, the Oblates continue to serve the people of God island-wide and abroad. With a particular missionary presence among Tamil-speaking people and communities across Sri Lanka, the Province seeks to proclaim the Good News, accompany people in their joys and struggles, and respond to the needs of the Church and society.

items.excerpt_en: Our missionary identity
items.body_en:
The Missionary Oblates of Mary Immaculate are a Roman Catholic missionary religious congregation founded by St Eugene de Mazenod. The Oblate vocation is rooted in the proclamation of the Gospel, especially among the poor and those most in need of hope, accompaniment and healing.

The Oblate Province of Jaffna is part of this worldwide missionary family. Its history in Sri Lanka reaches back to 1847, when the first Oblates arrived in Ceylon. In Jaffna, the mission developed through language learning, pastoral presence, education, formation, village ministry and accompaniment of communities through times of peace, suffering and social change.

items.excerpt_en: Evangelizing the poor
items.body_en: For the Oblate, the poor are not simply people who lack material resources. Poverty can also appear through abandonment, exclusion, displacement, addiction, disability, loneliness, injustice, conflict and loss of hope. Evangelizing the poor therefore means going towards people, listening to them, walking with them and proclaiming the Good News through word and life.

items.excerpt_en: A healing society through the Good News
items.body_en: Empowered by the Good News, we work for a healing society in and through the light of the Good News.

items.excerpt_en: A renewed, just and free society
items.body_en: A life towards a renewed, just and free society.

items.excerpt_en: Our founder and inspiration
items.body_en:
Eugene de Mazenod looked at a society marked by poverty, religious decline and social change and refused to remain indifferent. He preached to the poor, accompanied young people, reached prisoners and sought ways to communicate the Gospel in language people could understand.

His missionary conviction was simple and demanding: the Gospel must go out. It must reach people where they are. This missionary spirit became the foundation of the Oblate vocation.

Eugene de Mazenod looked at a society marked by poverty, religious decline and social change and refused to remain indifferent. He preached to the poor, accompanied young people, reached prisoners and sought ways to communicate the Gospel in language people could understand.

The mission moved beyond the city into villages, coastal communities and islands, reaching places such as Mannar, Point Pedro and Mullaitivu. Missionaries celebrated Mass, preached, baptized, visited families, taught children, formed catechists and helped establish Christian communities.

items.body_en: From parishes and schools to youth centres, counselling, rehabilitation, peacebuilding, community development, formation and diaspora ministry, the Province serves in many places and through many forms of missionary presence.
